title: Giant Propel Review: The Best Value Aero Bike in 2023?

takeaways.text: His SRAM Force AXS build with carbon wheels weighed 7.8 kg; Giant claims a 6.2 W aero saving at 40 km/h, 9.2% more frame stiffness and 85% more compliance than the previous Propel.

Hoses now run under the stem into a D-shaped steerer instead of the old over-stem routing; the two-piece cockpit only accepts Giant's own stems, and the stock bar is wider than he would like on an aero bike.
Clearance is up to 30 mm, and geometry now matches the TCR; the stock 25 mm tires and 10–33 cassette are the parts he would change first.

A big step up in comfort over the old Propel but still very stiff, especially around the bottom bracket; faster and more efficient than his TCR on the same wheels, though the TCR feels livelier on climbs.

disclosure: How the test bike was supplied is not stated. The bike reviewed is the third-generation Propel Advanced (same Advanced-grade frame family and 30 mm clearance as the candidate) with SRAM Force AXS, not the candidate's Tiagra build.
summary: A ride review of the 2023 third-generation Giant Propel Advanced, compared with the reviewer's own TCR Advanced.
